subject: Day 73: hidden-toy reach
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is starting to reach with intent and anticipate routines. Today's lead is a simple object-permanence precursor that pairs reaching with cause and effect.

Action items
- Partly hide a toy under a blanket, leaving an edge visible, and see whether Avi reaches for the exposed part. Full object permanence does not consolidate until eight to 10 months, so partial reaching now is the developmentally appropriate target. HealthyChildren movement: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Keep the freezer-stash pumping rhythm going if return-to-work is on the calendar; consistency over the next few weeks matters more than any single big session.
- Note when his longest night stretch lands each night so the emerging pattern is documented before the 4-month visit.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Bringing both hands to his mouth and looking at his hands with interest; this is expected hand-discovery, not a feeding cue.
- [monitor] Persistent asymmetric movement that consistently favors one arm or leg; document and raise at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] A new persistent crying pattern, or persistent feeding refusal.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, an apnea episode, or seizure-like activity. Call 911 immediately for blue lips or labored breathing!

Enrichment opportunities
- Set up the hidden-toy reach as a motor goal: place the visible edge just past his reach so he stretches and pivots toward it. HealthyChildren movement: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Let him visually track the toy as it disappears under the cloth and reappears, narrating where it went to tie vision to language. HealthyChildren baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Pair a sound, a soft rattle or a clap, with each reveal to add a cause-and-effect layer he can begin to predict. Music and infant cognition study: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; start a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (4-month visit): RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
